In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphonate analog of adenylylyl-(3,5)-adenosine isomerizes to adenylyl(2',5')adenosine via an intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the 3'-oxygen of the adenosine residue on the P-CH 2 bond.
the isomerization of internucloesidic 3',5' and 2',5' phosphonates to their 2'5' and 5',3' counterparts proceeds via a phosphorane intermediate.

the isomerization of internuleosidic phosphonate link- ages to the corresponding 2',5' counterparts can occur by several different mechanisms, depending on the nature of the phosphonate and the conditions employed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the isomerization of the internucleosidically bound phosphonate linkage is a facile process, and the rate of isomerization is dependent on the nature of the internucleotide linkages and on the pH-range.
the 3'-O- P -C H 2 -5'-phosphonate linkage is more stable than the 3'- O - P -C H (OH)-5'-phosphonoate linkage, which is more stable than its corresponding 2',5' linkage.
a hydrogen bond between a dianionic phosphonate and an adjacent hydroxy group is a prerequisite for the hydroxide-ion catalysis of isomerization of internuclear internucleosidyl phosphonates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the phosphonate linkage in the 3'-O-(CH 2 )-5'-position is much more stable than the 3'-phosphodiester linkage, and thus the phosphonate analog of adenylylyl-(3'-5')-adenylyl is a very good substrate for enzymatic reactions.
the 3',5'-phosphonate linkages are much more labile than the 2',5' counterparts.

the 3'-O-phosphono-5' linkage is a more stable bond than the 2'-O-phospho-5' linkage, which is consistent with the observed greater stability of the internucleosidically linked 2'-O-5' linkage in DNA compared to the 3'- O -5' linkage.
